commitResults.messageBody:
Move command reading, separators, greetings, task-result messages, and error reporting out of Sumo so the main class can focus on application flow. Pass the Ui dependency to the remaining command and loading routines without changing console behavior.

Update the documented Java 25 compile command and record that all nine exact console UI cases still pass. This establishes the first small OOP increment toward separating UI, storage, parsing, and task-list responsibilities.

Move the data-file path, directory setup, atomic writes, tolerant loading, and stored-task reconstruction out of Sumo. Inject one Storage instance into command handling so every task mutation keeps the existing save-and-rollback behavior.

Keep user-command parsing in Sumo for the later Parser increment, update the Java 25 compile command, and record all nine exact UI tests including every immediate persistence assertion.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract user command parsing into Parser
commitResults.messageBody: Move command recognition, argument validation, task construction, and date/time conversion out of Sumo. Return structured parsed commands so the main class can focus on coordinating UI, task mutations, and storage while preserving existing behavior. Update the documented UI compile command and record all nine Java 25 regression checks.

Move ordered task storage, mutation operations, and date filtering out of Sumo and into a dedicated TaskList abstraction. Keep save coordination and rollback in Sumo so the collection remains independent of persistence concerns, and expose read-only snapshots to callers.

Update the console UI test plan compile command and record the Java 25 exact-output regression run, including intermediate persistence, restart, and missing-directory checks.

Store Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList as application fields initialized by a file-path constructor. Move the command loop into run() and convert command handlers to instance methods so they use the coordinator's collaborators without repeatedly passing them as parameters.

Keep main() as a minimal entry point using the default data path, and record the complete Java 25 console regression run in the UI test plan.

Add an abstract Command contract and extract ExitCommand, ListCommand, and OnCommand as the first concrete command classes. Update Parser to return commands and simplify Sumo.run() so it executes commands uniformly and checks isExit() instead of switching on command types.

Keep add, delete, mark, and unmark behavior in a transitional ParsedCommand implementation so those state-changing operations can be extracted safely in later increments without changing persistence rollback behavior. Update and run the complete Java 25 UI test plan.

continuation and switch indentation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix documentation and test source coverage
commitResults.messageBody:
Javadoc generation reports incomplete API documentation, and the UI test runner sits outside Gradle's test source set. This leaves documentation warnings and excludes the runner from normal compilation and Checkstyle checks.

Document the affected public API and register the test directory with Gradle so the full verification workflow covers the runner.

Add an FXML-based chat window while preserving Sumo's existing
command and storage behavior.

Keep avatar resources optional so students can add their own images

Document the GUI workflow and cover the response adapter with tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor task types into an enum
Parser: Use varargs for command splitting

commitResults.messageBody:
Task construction, collection operations, command parsing, and storage rely on non-null, index, and date-precision assumptions. Make these assumptions explicit with assertion checks so development runs can expose invalid internal state early.

Keep user-input and persisted-record validation as exceptions, since those are expected runtime errors rather than programmer failures. Preserve the existing behavior while checking command representations, task persistability, collection contents, and storage reconstruction.

Task currently exposes its description and completion state to subclasses through protected fields, even though task types already use the public task operations. Make the description final and both fields private so future subclasses cannot bypass the task API. Preserve the existing behavior and display formats while reducing accidental coupling.

Ui repeats the same one-based task-numbering loop in three display methods, so formatting changes can drift between list views. Extract the shared loop into one private helper and keep each public method responsible only for its heading. This preserves the existing console output while making the presentation logic consistent.

Parser repeats command-prefix checks and relies on numeric substring offsets that hide which keyword each offset belongs to. Use a shared command-boundary check and derive argument positions from the keyword length. Keep argument-bearing commands and exact commands distinct so the accepted input remains unchanged while the parsing flow becomes easier to read and extend.

Storage reconstructs tasks using positional indexes and raw completion-status literals, which makes the persistence format harder to understand and maintain. Name the record positions, statuses, and separator, then use those names throughout validation and reconstruction. Keep the file format and loading behavior unchanged while making the serialization contract explicit.

Task serialization uses raw status codes and repeated separators, which hides the meaning of the stored values from readers. Introduce descriptive constants and build the record from a named completion status. Preserve the existing storage format while making the persistence code self-documenting.

Storage.parseTask validates records, constructs each task subtype, and restores completion state in one method, which mixes several abstraction levels. Extract validation, construction, and status restoration so the method reads as a short reconstruction workflow. Preserve all validation messages, task types, and completion behavior.

Parser.parse handles six command categories in a single long chain, which makes the dispatch logic harder to scan and mixes abstraction levels. Group query, indexed-task, and task-creation branches into focused helpers while retaining the same command precedence and validation messages. Keep the public parse entry point as the concise overview of the parsing workflow.

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskList: Use streams for task filtering
commitResults.messageBody: Task filtering and task-type lookup use explicit iteration, even though both operations are collection transformations. Refactor the task searches and storage-code lookup to use sequential streams for clearer filtering intent. Collect search results into ArrayList instances so encounter order, mutable return values, and matching behavior remain unchanged. Preserve the existing exception for unknown task type codes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle invalid input and protect saved task data
commitResults.messageBody:
Invalid event ranges and duplicate tasks can enter the task list.
Failed or partial loads can also allow later changes to overwrite
saved data that the session did not successfully load.

Validate command parameters, dates, event ranges, and duplicate task
details while accepting extra horizontal whitespace. Explain failures
without ending the session, and surface loading warnings in the GUI.

Disable saving after incomplete loads and reject externally changed
files to preserve recoverable data. Retain rollback on failed writes
and document the validation rules and recovery steps.

Verify with 62 passing JUnit tests, both Checkstyle checks, and all
14 console UI cases on Java 25. Use the user-level Gradle cache to
avoid an access error in the project-local JavaFX dependency cache.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for core application behavior
commitResults.messageBody:
The core model, query commands, and console output have testable
behavior that was not covered directly. This makes regressions harder to
identify and localize.

Add focused JUnit tests for task validation and formatting, task-type
metadata, non-mutating commands, and UI responses. Keep JavaFX-specific
behavior outside this automated suite because it requires a graphical
runtime.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use normal Gradle cache in Codex
commitResults.messageBody:
Codex builds that use a repository-local Gradle cache can encounter
Windows file permission errors while reading cached JARs.

Direct Codex to use the normal user-level cache on Windows and avoid
creating .gradle-user inside the repository.

The additional automated coverage belongs on master without including
the later Codex configuration change.

Merge the focused command, task, task-type, and UI tests while keeping
the feature branch history visible.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix usability issues found in smoke-test reports
commitResults.messageBody:
Smoke-test reports highlight windows that remain open after bye,
case-sensitive searches, and unclear empty results. Sumo shares
these usability gaps, and its launch documentation is outdated.

timer, make find ignore capitalization, and explain empty results.

record the forum findings and remaining platform-test limitations.
